subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Charging Curve
description: Learn The Charging Curve in one minute.

hook.text: Fast charging an EV is not like filling a gas tank—the speed drops dramatically as the battery fills up.

buildup.text: From 10 to 50 percent, fast chargers pump energy in at maximum speed with almost no resistance.

discovery.text: Above 80 percent, charging slows to a crawl because pushing more ions in risks overheating the cells.

twist.text: That's why the advice is to charge to 80 percent on road trips—the last 20 takes as long as the first 60.

climax.text: Understanding the charging curve saves enormous time on long trips compared to charging to 100 each stop.

punchline.text: The fastest strategy is to stop charging before the battery is full.

quiz.question: Why does EV fast charging slow down above 80 percent?
options: The charger runs out of power
Pushing more ions risks overheating the cells
The car's computer limits it for no reason
